column1: # The pieces that the names of NVIDIA for SASS hold, read by whatever names a form of the .khw of the part. The build
# compiles nothing here in. Every piece is as the compiler of NVIDIA spells it. Thus what we write can go against
# what it writes, word for word.
# A form takes its name from what the part answered of it, never from a listing. The name is the type of value that its
# cases hold, the relation that it answers, and how many sources its fields hold. Then each qualifier that the
# answers of the part read it into, each after a dot, in the order of the rows below.
# IADD3 is an integer add of three sources, and IADD3.X takes the carry that an earlier one left. ISETP.GE.U32.AND
# compares as unsigned words, and joins its flag to another. The type is the row whose reads hold the relation. A
# relation that no type row reads takes none: S2R, not IS2R.
# Each row is a kind, then `<piece>`, `<reads>` and `<gloss>`, with a tab between each two. The kinds:
# - `type`: the type of value that the cases of the form hold.
# - `operation`: the relation that it answers, a ladder relation or a word of the high order language.
# - `count`: how many sources its fields hold, where NVIDIA writes the count.
# - `qualifier`: what its answers read it into, a coherence category or a word of the high order language.
# - `mark`: the mark that NVIDIA writes before the operand at the second word of the relation. That is where it writes
#   the relation as another one, with that operand marked.
# - `test`: the test that a comparison makes, after the operation and before the qualifier.
# - `join`: how the flag of a comparison joins the predicate that it reads, written last.
# - `order`: the order of the operands of a comparison in its text, one character for each operand.
# `<reads>` names what puts the piece in the name: ladder.<relation> (ladder.h), hol.<word> (gnascor_hol_lng.tsv), or
# <set> (the coherence sets of the query protocol table, P13)
